title: have
summary: **have** и **have got** (иметь, болеть), прошедшее **had**, а также **have** в значениях «есть, пить, принимать» (have breakfast, have a shower) — здесь have got нельзя.
ru:
## have и have got: иметь
Говоря о том, что у нас есть, можно использовать **have** или **have got** — смысл тот же.
> I **have** a new car. = I**'ve got** a new car. — У меня новая машина.
> Sue **has** long hair. = Sue **has got** long hair. — У Сью длинные волосы.
> **Do** they **have** any children? = **Have** they **got** any children?
> Tim **doesn't have** a job. = Tim **hasn't got** a job.
> How much time **do** you **have**? = How much time **have** you **got**?
То же и с болезнями:
> I **have** a headache. = I've got a headache. — У меня болит голова.
> **Do** you **have** a cold? = **Have** you **got** a cold? — У тебя простуда?
Другие: toothache, a cough, a sore throat, a temperature (температура), flu (грипп).

## Прошедшее: had (без got)
В прошедшем времени говорим **had**; вопрос и отрицание — с **did**. **Had got** обычно не используют.
> When I met Sue, she **had** short hair. — Когда я познакомился с Сью, у неё были короткие волосы.
> He **didn't have** any money. — У него не было денег.
> **Did** you **have** a good time? — Ты хорошо провёл время?

## have в значении «есть, пить, принимать, проводить»
В этих выражениях have значит **есть / пить / принимать / проводить**. **Have got** здесь **нельзя**.
- еда и питьё: **have** breakfast / lunch / dinner, a sandwich, a cup of coffee, something to eat
- действия: **have** a shower, a bath, a rest, a swim, a walk, a look
- события: **have** a party, a holiday, a nice time, a baby, an accident, a dream
> 'Where's Ann?' 'She's **having** lunch.' — Она обедает.
> I don't usually **have** breakfast. — Я обычно не завтракаю.
> We're **having** a party next week. — На следующей неделе у нас вечеринка.
> **Have** a nice time! — Хорошо вам повеселиться!
- ~~I've got breakfast at eight.~~ → I **have** breakfast at eight.
- ~~She's having long hair.~~ → She **has** (got) long hair. (в этом значении не используем -ing)

## Типичные ошибки
- ~~Do you have got a pen?~~ → **Do you have** a pen? / **Have you got** a pen?
- ~~I haven't breakfast.~~ → I **don't have** breakfast.
- ~~I had got a headache yesterday.~~ → I **had** a headache yesterday.
en:
## have and have got: possession
When we talk about things we own or characteristics, we can use **have** or **have got**. The meaning is the same.
> I **have** a new car. = I**'ve got** a new car.
> Sue **has** long hair. = Sue **has got** long hair.
> **Do** they **have** any children? = **Have** they **got** any children?
> Tim **doesn't have** a job. = Tim **hasn't got** a job.
> How much time **do** you **have**? = How much time **have** you **got**?
It is the same for illnesses:
> I **have** a headache. = I've got a headache.
> **Do** you **have** a cold? = **Have** you **got** a cold?
Also: toothache, a cough, a sore throat, a temperature, flu.

## Past: had (without got)
> When I met Sue, she **had** short hair.
> He **didn't have** any money.
> **Did** you **have** a good time?

## have = eat, drink, take, spend
In these expressions we **cannot** use have got.
- food and drink: **have** breakfast / lunch / dinner, a sandwich, a cup of coffee, something to eat
- actions: **have** a shower, a bath, a rest, a swim, a walk, a look
- events: **have** a party, a holiday, a nice time, a baby, an accident, a dream
> 'Where's Ann?' 'She's **having** lunch.'
> I don't usually **have** breakfast.
> We're **having** a party next week.
> **Have** a nice time!
- ~~I've got breakfast at eight.~~ → I **have** breakfast at eight.

## Common mistakes
- ~~Do you have got a pen?~~ → **Do you have** a pen? / **Have you got** a pen?
- ~~I haven't breakfast.~~ → I **don't have** breakfast.
- ~~I had got a headache yesterday.~~ → I **had** a headache yesterday.
structure:
## have / have got (иметь)
| | have | have got |
|---|---|---|
| Утверждение | I have a bike. | I've got a bike. |
| (he / she / it) | She has a bike. | She's got a bike. |
| Отрицание | I don't have a bike. | I haven't got a bike. |
| (he / she / it) | He doesn't have a bike. | He hasn't got a bike. |
| Вопрос | Do you have a bike? | Have you got a bike? |
| (he / she / it) | Does she have a bike? | Has she got a bike? |

## Прошедшее время
| Утверждение | Отрицание | Вопрос |
|---|---|---|
| I had a bike. | I didn't have a bike. | Did you have a bike? |

## have = есть, пить, принимать (только have, без got)
| Вопрос / отрицание | Пример |
|---|---|
| Do you have breakfast? | I don't have breakfast. |
| Did you have a shower? | We didn't have a party. |

## Памятка
> **have got** — только для «иметь» и болезней (настоящее время).
> **have breakfast / a shower / a party** — только **have** (+ do/did в вопросе и отрицании).
